reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that racetrack betting markets can be modeled as a mixture of independent and herding agents. Independent agents base bets on private information (true winning probabilities), while herding agents mimic current popularity. By analyzing how implied probabilities converge over time, one can extract the convergence exponent β. This β relates directly to the fraction of independent agents through r_i = β/2. In the JRA dataset, β = 0.488 yields r_i ≈ 0.244, implying a 1:3 ratio of independent to herding bettors. The model assumes that the market dynamics follow a power-law convergence, which allows inversion of the relationship to estimate information content. The key mathematical structure is the squared deviation (x_t^w - w)^2 ~ t^{-2r_i}, which governs how quickly beliefs align. When r_i < 0.5, super-diffusion occurs, meaning convergence is slower. The model also incorporates a gamma prior for w, reflecting uncertainty in initial beliefs. This framework enables GSE to classify NFL line movements based on whether they resemble independent or herding behavior, informing adaptive betting strategies.
